hero.lead: A nation of 135.5 million on Africa’s great highland plateau, whose energy is almost entirely renewable and whose reform programme the IMF has backed with $3.4 billion.

capital.heading: Ethiopia runs one of Africa’s largest reform programmes. Next, a clean stove in every home.

register.name: Urban Productive Safety Net and Jobs Project, additional financing
register.detail: Signed January 2026 · Ministry of Finance and the World Bank
register.note: Public works, livelihood grants and youth jobs in towns
register.text: Additional World Bank financing for labour-intensive public works, livelihood grants, youth employment and cash transfers for poor and vulnerable urban households, including refugees and host communities. It serves the food and livelihood standards in the cities.

register.name: Productive Safety Net Project 6
register.note: Short-term work for six million people
register.text: Pays food-insecure households for public works and helps 700,000 people start small businesses.

register.name: Clean energy access (ASCENT Ethiopia)
register.text: Connects households, businesses and towns to the grid, aiming at six million people.

register.name: Development Policy Operation
register.text: Backs the reforms that opened the economy to investment and stabilised prices.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.note: About $464 million released in July 2026; about $2.6 billion disbursed in total
register.text: A four-year programme behind the float of the birr and the restructuring of the nation’s debts.

register.name: First Sustainable and Inclusive Growth Development Policy Operation
register.detail: Approved 30 July 2024 · $1B IDA grant and $500M IDA credit · Budget support
register.note: The first World Bank reform operation
register.text: Budget support for reforms to the financial sector, trade, fiscal transparency and state-owned enterprises, and for wider safety nets for poor and vulnerable households. It also backs sustainable land and forest management and access to renewable energy.

register.name: South Sudan-Ethiopia-Djibouti Transport Corridor, Phase II
register.detail: Approved 3 December 2025 · Grants from the concessional window · $214.47M for three nations
register.note: Ethiopia’s share: an expressway, feeder roads, a training centre
register.text: The Ethiopian part of the African Development Bank’s corridor grants: a 67 km expressway, intelligent transport systems, 50 km of feeder roads and a new automotive and engineering technical and vocational training centre. It includes training for 300 women and young people in Ethiopia.

register.name: Borana Resilient Water Development for Improved Livelihoods Programme II, additional financing
register.detail: Announced 21 October 2025 · $9.38M ADF Climate Action Window grant and $7M Rome Process/Mattei Plan facility
register.note: Clean water for 23,000 more people in Borana
register.text: Solar-powered water systems and about 95 km of new distribution network in Borana, Oromia, run by the Ministry of Water and Energy, with household biogas units and watershed management. Clean water for 23,000 more people and 50,000 livestock: the water and livelihood standards.

register.name: Aysha Wind Power Project, 300 MW
register.detail: Approved 15 July 2026 · $80M AfDB, $20M Clean Technology Fund, $10M SEFA · Total cost about $508M · 25-year power purchase agreement
register.note: A 300 MW independent wind power project
register.text: African Development Bank financing for a 300 MW wind farm near Aysha in the Somali Region, developed, owned and operated by AMEA Power, with the IFC as co-mandated lead arranger. Ethiopian Electric Power is the sole buyer of about 1,189 GWh a year, the energy standard.

register.name: Alema Koudijs Feed, IFC loan in birr
register.detail: Approved 4 June 2026 · Signed 4 September 2026 · Invested 7 October 2026 · Total project cost about $12.3M
register.note: A larger feed mill and new silos in Bishoftu
register.text: An IFC loan in Ethiopian birr, backed by IDA’s Private Sector Window, for the expansion of a compound feed mill owned by De Heus Animal Nutrition and Alema Farms. Better feed for poultry and livestock farmers supports the food standard.

register.name: MIDROC Ethiopia, IFC loan for the Sheraton Addis
register.detail: Approved 27 May 2026 · Signed 29 May 2026 · Invested 11 September 2026 · Total project cost up to $116M
register.note: Hotel refurbishment and a new hotel in Addis Ababa
register.text: An IFC loan for the refurbishment of the Sheraton Addis and a new Sheraton hotel in Addis Ababa, with green building certification. The IFC expects more formal employment and local value added in the hospitality sector: the livelihood standard.

register.name: Dashen Bank, risk-sharing facility for small businesses
register.detail: Announced 17 February 2026 · IFC covers 50% of a portfolio of up to $20M · First-loss guarantee from the IDA18 IFC-MIGA Private Sector Window
register.note: Loans to agribusiness and women-led firms
register.text: An unfunded IFC risk-sharing facility that lets Dashen Bank lend to more small and medium enterprises, with a focus on agribusiness and businesses owned or led by women. Credit for small firms supports the livelihood standard.

register.name: VisionFund Microfinance, IFC loan in birr
register.detail: Announced 8 September 2025 · First tranche of a planned $30M commitment
register.note: At least half for women-owned businesses
register.text: A local-currency IFC loan to Ethiopia’s largest privately held deposit-taking microfinance institution, to widen lending to micro, small and medium enterprises across the country, especially in rural areas. At least half of the proceeds go to businesses owned by women: the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 24 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A market square in an Ethiopian highland town

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Terraced green highland farmland and teff fields in Ethiopia

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Montane forest around an Ethiopian Orthodox church in the highlands

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: The Blue Nile Falls in the Ethiopian highlands

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2020
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam on the Blue Nile, wide view

items.name: Alema Koudijs Feed
items.text: A compound feed producer in Bishoftu, owned by De Heus Animal Nutrition and Alema Farms, expanding its feed mill and building new silos with an IFC loan; it makes compound feed for poultry and livestock farmers.

items.name: Hamlin Fistula Ethiopia
items.text: Six fistula hospitals, led from the Addis Ababa Fistula Hospital opened in 1974, the Hamlin College of Midwives and more than 90 supported midwifery clinics; its clinical team has treated more than 82,000 Ethiopian women.

items.name: VisionFund Microfinance
items.text: Ethiopia’s largest privately held deposit-taking microfinance institution, lending to micro, small and medium enterprises across the country, with at least half of a new IFC loan for businesses owned by women.
